title: Transposed coefficient mate identity for proper/open interchange
statement: Let A and B be finite commutative rings with a ring map φ, and let k : U ↪ V, r : U → W, p : V → Z, and i : W ↪ Z be a cartesian square. For E in the derived category of A-modules on U satisfying the stated lower-bound hypotheses (and whose scalar extension also satisfies a lower bound), apply the inverse of the proper direct-image adjunction Hom-equivalence for p to the coefficient interchange composite. The resulting transpose equals the inverse-adjunction transpose of properOpenCoefficientComposite φ sq E.

source.place: Tags 0F7B and 0GL6; blueprint main-20261015 sec-smooth-purity coefficient mate, Step 1 (mate-pasting identity after proper adjunction).

proof.text: Identify restriction of coefficients with the canonical uniqueness-of-left-adjoints comparison, and prove its ordinary pullback square coherence by conjugation. Descend the coherent cube to exact unbounded derived functors with mapDerivedCategory_exactCube. Taking inverse scalar-adjunction mates gives the scalar/pullback cube. Transport from left-derived pullback to exact derived pullback, and characterize finiteCoefficientDirectImageMap by its scalar-unit equation to identify it with the geometric mate of the inverse scalar comparison. Mate-pasting then gives exact exchange compatibility with coefficients.

For an open immersion compare the coefficient restriction isomorphism with the general pullback coefficient isomorphism: the two composite restriction/coextension adjunctions have equal units, by sectionwise naturality. Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies their comparisons. The defining uniqueness formula for openScalarExtension gives its inverse-unit formula. The recorded proper/open theorem normalizes its restriction as the inverse exchange followed by the open unit. Prove the desired coefficient square by cancellation of the open scalar isomorphism, the open Hom equivalence, and the invertible exchange at the extension by zero; use exchange compatibility, the two scalar/open unit equations, and naturality. Apply the inverse proper Hom equivalence to this equality.

theorem properOpen_coefficient_mate_transposed
    {A B : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Finite A] [Finite B]
    (φ : A →+* B) (sq : IsPullback k r p i) (E : DerivedCategoryModule A U)
    (_hE : ∃ n : ℤ, E.IsGE n)
    (_hEB : ∃ n : ℤ, ((scalarExtension φ U).obj E).IsGE n) :
    let adj := derivedUpperStarLowerStarAdjunction (ModuleCat.{u + 1} B) p
    ((adj.homEquiv _ _).symm)
      ((scalarExtension φ Z).map ((properOpenCoefficientInterchange A sq).hom.app E) ≫
        finiteCoefficientDirectImageMap φ p
          (D((k)_!open[ModuleCat.{u + 1} A]).obj E) ≫
        R((p)_*[ModuleCat.{u + 1} B]).map
          ((openScalarExtension φ k).hom.app E)) =
    ((adj.homEquiv _ _).symm)
      (properOpenCoefficientComposite φ sq E)
